*UPDATED REVIEW BELOW* I'm only 3 hours in, but so far I don't understand a lot of the negativity others have toward this game.  I've completed the first two areas and defeated the first two bosses.  Just so you know, I *hated* Dark Souls... I found it to be far too punishing and the overall look and feel didn't do much for me.  That said, I've loved several "souls-likes", such as Lords of the Fallen and The Surge. So it goes without saying I'm not a Souls purist, but I have so far enjoyed several similar games that weren't quite as punishing and had a more pleasing aesthetic.   This game doesn't quite rise to the level of LotF or Surge in my opinion, but it's decent.  The color palette consists of too many greens and greys so far for my taste, but the trailers and screenshots show some diversity to the worlds, so I'm looking forward to some different scenery.  The sci-fi/fantasy mishmash is interesting, however, and the world reflects a certain HR Geiger look that's kind of cool.  The story so far as pretty much nonsense, but at least it has a story.  

Overall, love or hate the style of the world, the graphics are so far decent, some of it looks like a last-generation game, but it's far from terrible.  The controls are responsive and simple enough, and while it might at first seem a flaw that locking onto targets requires you to be a certain distance, this is actually a function of the equipped weapon's stats.  Music is there, and it's appropriately brooding, and fortunately there's normally not long sections of silence like Souls. Not great music like LotF, but good enough.  Soundtrack is a free download if you buy the game, whoopee.  The gunplay isn't bad, and the lock-on feature helps quite a bit, so enable it.  There's not a lot of ways to get more ammo, and I foolishly used the three ammo packs you start off with thinking like medkits they'd refill at a save point, but they did not.  This means some survival game style ammo conservation, which leads to fun little strategies like shotgunning enemies within an inch of their life and then finishing them off by rushing in with a melee attack to save a shell.  Some have said it's odd that all the enemies have "targets" on their backs that are vulnerable, but nobody seemed to take issue with the idea that back attacks in Souls resulted in huge damage... This is really no different.

On the negative side, there are too many stats to level up, and the distinction between them is muddy, and the symbols that correspond to them are unhelpful.  Different weapons require different stats, and if you try to make a balanced character you're going to have a hard time equipping anything because there's little rhyme or reason to what each one needs.  Basically you need to throw a lot of points on a handful of stats and hope.

So far difficulty is what I'd call a fair challenge without being punishing.  The need to collect tokens of sorts to open some chests is a bit weird and annoying, it often makes me wonder if I've missed a token or if I'm not supposed to be able to open a chest yet.

All in all, I give it a 7/10 so far.  Not great, just pretty good.  If you like Souls-likes and don't mind something with a different take and ranged combat, this might be for you.

==UPDATE==

11 hours in now, well into the third/fourth sections of the game... haven't found the third boss yet, but I believe I'm close.  Difficulty ramps up after the first two areas, but careful exploration is rewarded with shortcuts, helpful treasure and hidden save points.  Only impossible seeming if you're in too big of a hurry or not paying attention to your surroundings.  You get additional med kit and grenade slots as you find "armor upgrades", which help quite a bit and regenerate at save points.  I will say that getting a sniper rifle and the stats to use it allows you to pull off some awesome feats and takes the difficulty down a notch.  I actually headshot a mini-boss from across a large room and he never touched me.  Some of the armored "knight" looking enemies are very cool.  Basically, the more I play the more I like it.  If it had a better soundtrack and a less scattershot stats/leveling system, I'd like it as well as the Surge and LotF at this point.  A good stop-gap game of this type while waiting on Surge 2. 
 Upgrading to 8/10.

Ive played the Souls games before and in comparison to this im not really that impressed like i was when i bought this game. I wanted a new challenge and a souls like game with guns felt like a exciting new way in this genre. When i first started the game and played the first level i was getting a bit dissapointed about the level design and the performance this game offers.
The levels are VERY small like not the size overall but 1 level feels like a coridor with like 1 a bit larger and open area thats it. There is just too little space to roll around the enemys. The next thing i have to critisize is the Performance and the bugs in this game. So the performance for me is absolutly terrible for the pc specs i have. Like i dont know how you can optimize a game like that. I have a i7 8700k and a GTX 1070 16gb RAM and in some places i get 35 Fps like this is just horrible and very bad made. The bugs are very significant and its just ruining the fun i had with the game in the first 20-30min. Fell of a cliff because the character bugged in the texture and i had to restart the whole thing again. The next thing i have to critisize is the animations and movement. For me personally everything feels very clunky and the animations are sometimes bugged and they are not smooth like in Dark Souls for example. If we talk about the general difficulty of the game without the bugs and glitches that make this game difficult enough already its very dissapointing again. Ive read a lot of comments and reviews regarding this game and a lot of people said its made intentionally hard and it feels like the developers just wanted the game experience to be a torture. Enemys are in complete random spots 5 enemys instantly shooting at you from 5 angles and btw the damage is just a complete joke. In the swap area the boss killed me with 1 hit when i had full hp. 

Overall the game is a big dissapointment for me interms of the general game experience and gameplay aspect and the performance is making it even worse.

Negatives:
- Very Clunky animations and sometimes they are bugged
- A lot of buggs and glitches 
- Performance is very bad for me at least
- Levels are made very small and coridor like so you have no chance to even use the dodge mechanics
- The positioning of the enemys is a complete joke 
- The difficulty of this game is just a torture 
-  Price is way to high for this game

Positives:
- First 20-30 min are ok to play
- Graphics is ok too but nothing that special
- The audio and music are well used

So to conclude this review i cant recomment this game until the most part of the buggs are fixed and the performance is getting improved A LOT. 

Score of the game 4/10

Ok, so yes, this is a souls like game. It isnt  the best clone, but by far not the worst. For better or worse, it did try to make itself stand out with a few interesting ideas.  Unlocking shortcuts requires items that can be spent elsewhere,  enemies with  tactical mechanics (IE one enemy can mark you with a homing beacon and all the other enemy shots will home in on you), and of course, the main way to take down enemies being weakspots on them. (always the back though). Is it perfect? No. Is it worth the full price? No. But if you are looking for a decent adventure shooter, I would honestly recommend if it is on sale

[h1] THIS REVIEW BROUGHT TO YOU BY YOUR RIGHTFUL RULER, THE OLD LORD OF THE DEEP REACHES, AND HIS EXCESSIVE USE OF CAPSLOCK TO PONTIFICATE HIS EMINANCE. (JOIN OUR CURATOR GROUP NOW, ALL SACRIFICES ACCEPTED.) [/h1]

[b] INITIAL OPINION [/b]

WHILST I AM NOT ONE FOR FOLLOWING A CROWD'S OPINION, I MUST ADMIT THIS GAME CERTAINLY WARRANTS THE HATE IT RECEIVES. BEING A BLATANT CLONE OF THE SOULS GENRE, THE LACK OF A PROPER PAUSE FEATURE FOR THE SAKE OF EMULATING THE MORE POPULAR SERIES REALLY TELLS THE STORY OF THIS GAME'S CONCEPTION. THE LESS-THAN-FINE-TUNED CONTROLS MADE THE FIRST BOSS A NIGHTMARE, COUPLED WITH HIS GODLIKE ABILITY TO ZERO IN MY LOCATION WITH EVERY BURST OF WEAPONS FIRE, MADE MY INITIAL EXPERIENCE A REFUND-TIER LETDOWN.

[u] POSITIVE ASPECTS [/u]

FIREARMS, I SUPPOSE. THE WEAPONS DO FEEL IMPACTFUL TO A POINT, AS WELL AS THE WORLD BEING AN INTERESTING LABYRINTHINE CYBERPUNK LAND OF DIGITAL PULSES AND MULTI-GOGGLE GLOWING-EYED ADVERSERIES.

[u] NEGATIVE ASPECTS [/u]

NEARLY EVERYTHING ELSE. LOOSE CONTROLS. LONG ARDUOUS ANIMATIONS. PINPOINT-ACCURATE ENEMIES RIVALING GODLIKE BOTS FROM UNREAL TOURNAMENT. THIS CONSTANT SENSE THAT THE DEVELOPERS TRIED MUCH TOO HARD TO MAKE THIS "DARK SOULS WITH GUNS" AS SOME OTHER PEASANT REVIEWERS STATED, SANS THE LACK OF A PAUSE FEATURE IN THIS [i] SINGLEPLAYER ONLY GAME. [/i] 

[b] CONCLUDING THOUGHTS [/b]

I CAN SEE MOUNTAINS OF POTENTIAL, BUT UNTIL THE DEVELOPERS TWEAK THE CONTROL SCHEME, AND IT'S ENEMIES, AND CAN UNDERSTAND THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN "SOULS-LIKE" AND "BLATANT SOULS COPY", THIS GAME AND IT'S FUTURE WILL END WITH THIS GAME, AND IT'S NEGATIVE REVIEW SCORE.

It’s a dark souls like game but with guns.

The game itself plays just like dark souls, no directions, no pause, die lose all your points but can recover them and so on. The gameplay is very solid, everything works smoothly from the rolling to even shooting. 

Some of the negative stuff I noticed about the game was the lack off bosses, your going to spend most of your time fighting mobs who can become very annoying if they have a shield which blocks everything. If you are dying to one of the bosses or just having bad luck, you will have to keep fighting these annoying mobs and don’t try to run past them they will just keep chasing you.

The game has a lot of guns ranging from pistols to even grenade launchers, but you will soon notice that some of these guns are 
not good, for example the assault rifles recoil is so bad, you will just end up just using snipers.

How much running you must do in this game is crazy also, your character movement speed is so slow without spirting and you don’t want to sprint everywhere because then you might run out of stamina.

Overall, it was a fun game when I first started it, the DLC boss was the hardest of them all. After I beat that every other boss was just 3-5 hits, I only used two snipers so it got very boring at the end. They do offer new game + but like I said, the mobs are annoying so who would want to fight through all those shields again?? Not me.

Everyone call this game 'Dark Souls with Guns'. As an avid dark souls fan, I wanted to check this game out, since I'm fairly new to third person shooters.
The things this game shares with dark souls is:
        Bonfire type Checkpoint System
        Loss of all Currency on Death
        Health Items/Ammo recharge when resting or Death
I would not put difficulty here, as the way that Immortal Unchained does difficulty is terrible.
        Enemies with pinpoint accuracy, 
        HOARDS of enemies
        High damage output
        No cover for you, some cover for enemies
This game ramps up difficulty by throwing more enemies at you. I looked at the run from the nearest 'Monolith' to the second boss fight. At a certain point their were no less than 4 mid-tier enemies and 2 low tier enemies in that one area. You have 1 piece of cover that is destroyed within seconds, because of the amount of fire you are taking. You must stay swift, dodging 4 automatic guns, as well as killing these enemies.
Don't even think of running away from them, because they will shoot you in the back.
Quantity over Quality. Its the same in Dark Souls 2. 
What people need to understand, is that difficulty is easy to implement. Just give the player 1 life, 1 hit until they die, and block their path with enemies so they must die. What isn't easy, is fair difficulty. And that is where this game fails.

I cannot recommend this game, I just can't. I looked through all the negative reviews, got this game half price, even that was too high. I find it really hard to push myself forward in this game when it's so punishing, and hardly even satisfying to complete, as you know as soon as you complete something, something even more b*llsh*t will arise.

If you really want to buy this game, I can't stop you, I should know. But don't go into this game thinking its fun.

Once you got to the minigun enemys that kill you instant over distance and are only vulnerable at their backs, it's just f*cking annoying! It had a good start though and was a nice soulslike to begin with. The bosses were fun and beatable and the level design was ok, but they destroyed the game for me completely...
